chunks.content: ## Opening and Preparing the Practice File in CLO This section covers how to locate and open the practice project file in CLO, including navigating folders and loading the file into the 3D workspace. - In the Library window, double-click to open the **practice** folder. - Navigate to the **C details** folder, then to the **B Constructing and Shoot Practice** folder. - Select the file named **Shoot Practice**. - Open the file by double-clicking or dragging it into the 3D window for editing. ## Creating Shirt Plackets Using Cut and Sew Tool This section explains the process of dividing a garment panel into plackets using the Cut and Sew tool, and how to adjust sewing lines automatically created between panels. - Use the **Loop Outline Tool** to select the purple baseline on the front panel. - Right-click on the selected line and choose **Cut and Sew** from the menu. - The front panel will be split into two sections along the selected line. - A sewing line is automatically created between the two new panels. ## Adjusting the Door Panel and Thickness Settings This section details how to adjust the size and thickness of the door panel to simulate realistic fabric layers and thickness in CLO. - In the 2D window, select the **door panel**. - Use the **Adjustment Panel Tool** to modify the panel shape as needed. - To simulate fabric thickness, set the thickness parameter: - In the Library window, locate the fabric thickness option at the bottom side panel. - Select the door panel again in the 2D window. - Enter the thickness value corresponding to the selected fabric to reflect realistic material depth. - To show a double-layer effect on a single-layer panel, enable the **Double-Layer Effect** option. - Assign the **outer layer** to the panel to simulate layered fabric visually. - Ensure the collar remains straight and aligned on top of the front panel. ## Editing Sewing Lines and Managing Seam Effects This section explains how to modify sewing lines, remove unwanted seam blurring, and apply effects to improve visual quality after simulation. - Select the **Edit Sewing Line Tool** in the 2D window. - Click on the sewing line along the collar area. - Press **Delete** to remove any blurring or seam artifacts. - Re-mix the seam blending carefully; avoid mixing on open edges. - In the **Sound Editor** (likely referring to the texture or surface editor), change the seam blurring type to **Tint**. - After running the **fire simulation** (simulation of fabric physics and rendering), the seams will appear more evenly blended. ## Applying Thickness and Button Effects in 3D Garment Simulation This section describes how to adjust button thickness and finalize thickness settings to enhance the 3D clothing simulation. - Open the **Object Window** and select the button object. - In the **Operation Editor**, adjust the button thickness parameter to the desired value. - Run the **fire simulation** to apply and visualize the changes in the 3D garment.
